claim: HA core abbreviations.py defines the complete legal set of abbreviated MQTT discovery keys, expanded by discovery.py before validation — keys such as avty_t (availability_topic), cmd_t (command_topic), stat_t (state_topic), uniq_id (unique_id), val_tpl (value_template), dev_cla (device_class), ent_cat (entity_category), en (enabled_by_default), pl_on/pl_off (payload_on/off), ret (retain) and '~' topic-base.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can emit abbreviated-key discovery payloads to minimise per-entity bytes across a fleet, validated against this exact table
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch abbreviations.py, 297 lines, 2026-09

claim: Device-block abbreviation keys include sn (serial_number), hw (hw_version), sw (sw_version), mf (manufacturer), mdl (model), cu (configuration_url) and ids/identifiers, and the origin block has its own abbreviation set (o/name, o/sw_version, o/support_url).
stance_target: ha-linux-agent discovery payloads can carry full device identity (hostname, NixOS version, hardware, config URL) compactly in the dev block
scope_conditions: HA core dev branch, DEVICE_ABBREVIATIONS and ORIGIN_ABBREVIATIONS tables

claim: The availability_mode option (abbreviated avty_mode) exists in the discovery schema, letting a device declare all/latest/any semantics when multiple availability topics are configured.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent can expose one shared status topic per host with latest/all semantics for multi-entity availability
